offence_severity: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both
number_of_offences: More than 102 sale deeds relating to the same transaction were executed
premeditation_planning: The respondent was alleged to have conspired and abetted in the commission of the crime
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the prima facie allegations that more than 102 sale deeds were forged to avail of the Special Rehabilitation Package meant for Project affected persons, and that the respondent was instrumental and abetted in the commission of the crime.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that the vendees and vendors were not Project affected persons but wanted to avail of the Package, thereby deceiving the State Government and Project affected persons.

legal_representation.accused: Sidharth Dave, Abhimanyu Singh, C.D. Singh

investigation_status: Charge-sheet filed against the respondent and others, investigation ongoing
procedural_irregularity: Procedural irregularities were found in the registration of sale deeds, including failure to verify the identity of the seller, not following Section 64 of the Registration Act, and not mentioning PAN Card numbers for deeds of valuation of Rs. Five lacs or more.

appeal_history.high_court: High Court quashed FIRs and charge-sheets, set aside judgments
appeal_history.supreme_court: Supreme Court allowed appeals, set aside High Court judgments

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the respondent, as Deputy Registrar, was instrumental in registering fraudulent sale deeds to avail of the Special Rehabilitation Package, thereby causing financial loss to the State Government and deceiving Project affected persons/oustees. The High Court's order to quash the FIRs and charge-sheets was deemed erroneous as the respondent's involvement needed to be determined based on evidence.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the respondent, as a Sub-Registrar, was only required to register documents and had no duty to verify the genuineness of the title or the authenticity of the parties involved. The High Court correctly noted that there were only procedural irregularities and no evidence of the respondent's direct involvement in the fraud.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the inherent power under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure should be exercised sparingly and with caution, and that the High Court should not quash criminal proceedings without sufficient evidence or material.
precedent_relied_upon: M. M. T. C. Ltd. & Anr. vs. Medchl Chemicals & Pharma (P) Ltd. & Anr. 2001 (5) Suppl. SCR 265; State of Orissa and Another v. Saroj Kumar Sahoo 2005 (5) Suppl. SCR 548; Eicher Tractors Ltd. v. Harihar Singh (2006) 12 SCC 763; Jambu Prasad v. Mohammad Nawab Aftab Ali Khan AIR 1941 PC 16
